summary: This diff adds a new, self-contained validator (ai-os-scripts/validate_dependency_graph.py) that re-derives, from real source (dispatchEngine() switch cases, registerGuardrail() call sites resolved through the file's own const/array indirection, and file-exists checks), whether each populated_route's expected_path hops actually match their claimed live_or_planned status, plus a whole-graph cross-check against the engines/gateways dependency table; it correctly reuses Phase 1's derive_dispatch_target() instead of duplicating it, and updates a new dependency_validation_status field in ROUTE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA via the same regex-scoped-block pattern used by prior phases. I ran the script live in the worker's own worktree: it executed cleanly (exit 0), reproduced the committed evidence exactly, and re-running it produced zero diff (idempotent). I independently verified the guardrail-leaf parser against every real registerGuardrail() call site in guardrail-registrations.ts (24/24 leaves resolved correctly, including both the scalar-const and array-for-loop indirection forms) and confirmed the honest cross-validation finding (route-implied engine edges 17->3, 3->8, 8->6, 3->9 vs. the documented table's 7 edges, zero overlap) is a real, not fabricated, gap. The diff is purely additive (new script, new evidence JSON files, new schema field + populated values, phase-plan status update), touches no migrations/schema/auth/security/permission/payment/billing/rls paths and no .github/workflows/** files, consistent with the tier1 classification. One minor, non-blocking design note: validate_hop()'s Rule Engine branch always checks the hardcoded guardrail-registrations.ts and ignores the hop's own declared mechanism_path (e.g. RT-gst_calculation_engine-001's hop cites business-rule-validator.ts); I confirmed by reading business-rule-validator.ts that this is currently safe because that file is just a thin evaluateGuardrails() pass-through with no leaf-specific logic of its own, but this coupling assumption isn't asserted or commented in the validator, so a future divergence between the two files would silently validate against the wrong mechanism.
issues: Minor: validate_hop()'s Rule Engine branch ignores the hop's declared mechanism_path and always checks guardrail-registrations.ts directly; currently correct because business-rule-validator.ts is a pure pass-through, but this assumption is undocumented in the code and would silently mis-validate if that coupling ever changes.
